Keeper of the wilderness, she represents the wild creatures of nature, the rush of the angry rapids, and the heat-harried stillness of the desert. Elves take up her worship, as do hunters of natural lands, accepting her guidance to exist harmoniously within savage lands. Those seeking safe passage across dangerous waters give prayers to her to guide them. The druids of the Wildmother and clerics of her lover, the Lawbearer, work together to preserve the balance of nature and civilization. It is said that the two goddesses grow furious when this balance is upset, and this fury manifests in Tal'Dorei as devastating natural disasters.

Seen immortalized through wooden reliefs and carved idols in hidden, overgrown groves and rural shrines, the Wildmother often is depicted as a beautiful woman of green skin nearly swallowed by a wild, tangled wreath of hair, leaves, and vines that dwarf her lithe form.

The Wildmother's holy day is Wild's Grandeur, and is celebrated on the vernal equinox, usually the twentieth day of the third month. The people of the southern wilds celebrate the Wildmother's strength by going on a journey to a place of great natural beauty, like the top of a mountain waterfall, or the center of a desert. Wild's Grandeur is rarely celebrated in Emon, but some folk will plant trees in observance of the holiday.

entries.name: Commandments of the Wildmother
items: {@i Protect the untamed wildernesses of the realm from exploitation and destruction.}
{@i Slay abominations and other dark mockeries of nature.}
{@i Embrace and respect the savage nature of the world. Exist in harmony with it.}

name: The Wildmother
symbol: A wreath of golden wheat with green leaves and red berries sprouting out of it. A wooden shepherd's staff is in the centre of the wreath, entwined with some vines.

symbolImg.altText: A wreath of golden wheat with green leaves and red berries sprouting out of it. A wooden shepherd's staff is in the centre of the wreath, entwined with some vines.

entries: The realm of the Wildmother extends to wherever the seas shift and the land grows over. As the keeper of the wilderness, she represents the wild creatures of nature, the rush of the angry rapids, and the heat-heavy stillness of the desert. Hunters, druids, and nomads worship her, seeking her blessing to live in harmony with lands that still bear their wild fangs. Likewise, those seeking safe passage across dangerous waters pray to her to guide them.

The druids of the Wildmother and clerics of her lover, the {@deity The Lawbearer|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Lawbearer}, work together to preserve the balance of nature and civilization. It is said that the two goddesses grow furious when this balance is upset, and this fury manifests as devastating natural disasters. Clerics of the {@deity The Matron of Ravens|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Matron of Ravens} also pay homage to the Wildmother, for the work she begins is the work that their deity must respectfully end.

entries.name: Depiction
entries: Immortalized through wooden reliefs and carved idols in hidden, overgrown groves and rural shrines, the Wildmother is shown as a beautiful woman with green or deep brown skin nearly swallowed by a wild, tangled wreath of hair, leaves, and vines that envelop her strong, full-figured form.

entries.name: Divine Domains
entries: Many of the Wildmother's clerics are granted powers of Life, Nature, or Tempest.

entries.name: Holy Day
entries: The Wildmother's holy day is Wild's Grandeur, and is celebrated on the vernal equinox, usually the twentieth day of the third month. The people of the southern wilds honor the Wildmother by journeying to a place of great natural beauty, like the top of a mountain waterfall or the center of a desert. Wild's Grandeur is rarely celebrated in {@book Emon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Emon, the City of Fellowship}, but some folk will plant trees in observance of the holiday.

entries.name: Commandments of the Wildmother
items: Protect the untamed wilderness from exploitation and destruction.
Slay abominations and other mockeries of nature.
Embrace and respect that which you cannot control in this world. Exist in harmony with it.

name: Thena
title: the Melancholy Gloom
symbol: A single tear
entries: Thena was one of the two first telorin to exist on Xhoria, the other being Auberon, her former husband. After Auberon abandoned her, a terrible depression overtook her. Umbrava took note of this event between Auberon and Thena, and given that Auberon was brought to divinity, he touched Thena and made her the deity of disorder and abandonment, a true embodiment of emotion and depression. Thena was thankful for the act of kindness Umbrava showed her. People that resonate with the events that Thena went through often pray to her for consolation.

name: Thessa
title: Goddess of Knowledge and the Sea
symbol: A dark blue trident

customProperties.Depiction: A human or Scyllaean elf woman holding a trident and a scroll or stone tablet
customProperties.Sacred Places: Lighthouses, harbors, the Acropolis of Ithea
customProperties.Worshipers: Scyllaean elves, sailors, philosophers, fishermen, explorers, merchants

entries: Thessa is the goddess of knowledge, magic, prophecy, and the sea. She is in the promise of the tide, the warm winds that bring sailors safely home, and the life-giving bounty of the sea. Hers are the arts of navigation, the stars, divination, arcana, and discovery.

name: Thor
title: The Thunderer
altNames: Slayer of Monsters and Protector of Mortals
Patron of the North, Dwarves, and Reavers
symbol: The hammer, a representation of Mjolnir
entries: Thor, the red-maned God of Thunder, is the boldest of Wotan's sons and the mightiest warrior in the heavens. Riding his chariot pulled by celestial goats and wielding the rune-etched hammer Mjolnir, he is the eternal foe of giants, trolls, and monsters. Thunder is his war cry, and lightning the swing of his arm. Though not known for wisdom, he possesses unmatched courage, good humor, and a roaring love of battle. When not battling foes, he dwells in his hall, Bilskirnir, with his wife Sif.

Thor appears as a burly, broad-shouldered man clad in sleeveless armor, with wild red hair and a beard like a blazing storm cloud. His eyes shine with fierce joy when battle calls. Around his waist is Megingjord, a magical belt of might inscribed with ancient runes, and Mjolnir always hangs at his side, short-hafted and thick-headed and radiating power.

entries.name: Worshipers
entries: Thor's followers are warriors, reavers, raiders, guards, and any who live by the strength of their arm. Dwarves are both wary and reverent of Thor. They honor him both as creator and protector, but some also believe he smote their empire during the Reaving for favoring Volund over him.
Everyone from raiders to farmers make offerings to Thor. Warriors look to him for strength and bravery, while peaceful folk display his hammer to ward off trolls and keep danger from their doors.

Thor teaches his faithful to believe strength is both virtue and weapon, and to meet every challenge head-on. To them, death in battle is the highest honor; Thor despises a "straw death" from age or illness. A popular battle cry to the storm god is "Thor's thunder in your ears!"

entries.name: Symbols and Books
entries: Thor's most sacred symbol is the hammer, a representation of Mjolnir, worn as a charm or painted on shields. He is associated with the rune Thurisaz. Many mortals, not just his worshipers, see storms as a symbol of Thor's will or wrath. Lightning is said to strike places of great valor or danger. Thunderstorms during births or duels are seen as blessings. In rural households, hammer-shaped charms are used to bless weddings, protect newborns, or keep trolls away from the hearth.

Those who follow Thor hold no faith in sacred books or tomes, preferring to tell stories and songs of his adventures around crackling fires with mugs of mead in hand. Some of the most popular are the Lay of Hymir, in which Thor catches Jormungandr on a fishing line, and Haustlong, where Thor battles a mighty jotun.

entries.name: Shrines and Priests
entries: Most shrines to Thor are open to the sky and often built atop windswept cliffs or along storm-wracked coastlines. Offerings of bear's blood, oxen, and shattered weapons are left upon the altar, preferably during thunderstorms. His greatest temple is the Hall of Golden Hammers in Thrumagard, led by Ulfrich Thorson, a famed dwarven priest of the Order of the Thunderer. Thor's clergy wear armor at all times and are taught to never refuse a challenge. They preach strength, honesty, and defiance in the face of evil. Sparring contests between Thor's priests and those of his wife Sif are common, testing whether brute strength or refined technique wins the gods' favor.

name: Thylea
title: Great Mother of All
symbol: Eternal golden ash tree
entries: Thylea is the namesake of the Lost Land. She takes the form of a gargantuan tree on an island at the heart of the Cerulean Gulf, and her followers believe that her roots reach deep into the earth, binding the world together in an eternal embrace. Thylea is believed to be a generous, life-giving goddess. The Druids of the Oldwood believe that her will is communicated through the changing of the seasons, rather than through words. Long winters, for example, signal her displeasure; long summers are a sign of her approval. She has been silent since the dawn of time, and as a consequence, very little is known about her.

It is known that she created the land eons ago. She is the lost sister of some elder pantheon. Unlike her siblings, she wished to live apart from the mortal races and created Thylea as a refuge from civilization. It was to be a place where nature and fey magic could flourish, without the corrupting influences of mortal desires. Accordingly, she created her own pantheon of Titans.

name: Thylea
title: Great Mother of All
symbol: Eternal golden ash tree
entries: Thylea is the namesake of the Lost Land. She takes the form of a gargantuan tree on an island at the heart of the Cerulean Gulf, and her followers believe that her roots reach deep into the earth, binding the world together in an eternal embrace. Thylea is believed to be a generous, life-giving goddess. The Druids of the Oldwood believe that her will is communicated through the changing of the seasons, rather than through words. Long winters, for example, signal her displeasure; long summers are a sign of her approval.

name: Thyr
title: God of Law and Justice; The Lawgiver; Tyr; Tiwaz
symbol: Silver cross on a white field

customProperties.Domains: {@class cleric|phb|Life|Life Domain}, {@class cleric|phb|Knowledge|Knowledge Domain}, {@class cleric|phb|Order|Order Domain|ggr}
customProperties.Form of Worship and Holidays: Worship services held on the last day of every month. Midwinter eve (called Commons) is set aside for the common folk to have their grievances heard before the highest courts of the land.
customProperties.Garb: White robes trimmed with silver, purple or gold—the colors of kingship
customProperties.Typical Worshipers: Human royalty, ruling and legislative bodies, some magistrates and judges

entries: Thyr is the god of wise and just rule. He is normally depicted as a wizened king seated on a great throne, holding the Rod of Kingship in one hand and the Chalice of Peace in the other. His principles are justice, order and peace. He represents proper and traditional rule and as such was once worshiped (at least in name) by all human royalty. He is the embodiment of the enlightened human caste system where each person has a fairly determined role in a lawful society intended to create the greatest good for the greatest number.

Thyr's symbol is a silver cross on a white field, symbolizing the upturned cross-haft of his sister's sword, which he thrust into the earth to end the Gods' War at the dawn of time. Upon seeing the blood of so many gods shed, Thyr foreswore the use of swords and his priests, for this reason, may not use bladed weapons. Many favor reinforced rods, similar to light maces, modeled after Thyr's own Rod of Kingship. The noble eagle and lion are his sacred creatures.

The Lawgiver, Thyr is a god that has transcended culture and appears in different aspects among different groups on the world of Lloegyr, spanning cultures from the Northlands to the Helcynngae Peninsula in the south. To Northlanders (and the Andøvan before them) he is known as Tiwaz and is depicted as having only one hand, the other having been bitten off by a powerful Godspawn of Chaos while Tiwaz distracted it and allowed it to be bound for the good of the world.

Thyr has actually been a part of the Hyperborean pantheon for thousands of years and for much of that empire's history was considered among its chief gods and most influential in its civilization alongside {@deity Muir|Lostlands|TheLostLands|Muir} and Arden (and later {@deity Solanus|Lostlands|TheLostLands|Solanus}). Thyr is also one of the ancient trinity of deities known as the Three Gods that predates the Hyperboreans. The Heldring venerate him as Tyr in much the same aspect as Thyr, though they depict him as one handed like Tiwaz.

It is unknown whether Thyr is truly a Northlands transplant or if his worship in fact developed concurrently but separately in the two different cultures. Or for that matter if it didn't develop long prior to either of them existing only to diverge somewhere along the way. In fact, it is not entirely certain that he is truly aspects of the same god (though the belief of that is near universal). Regardless, Thyr does not seem to raise any objection to the correlation, and his Thyr identity has by far been his largest church historically. The modern Heldring have formed an almost-theocratic society devoted to Tyr and Eostre (their name for Muir), and their hledwalda petitions annually for the High Altar of Thyr to be moved from Bard's Gate to Kingsgardt in the Kingdom of the Helcynn, while the empress of the actual-theocracy of Alcaldar likewise presses for it to be established in the imperial capital of Mhaltra. To date Thyr's clergy have remained silent on the subject of relocation, though patience wears thin among the royalties of those respective nations.

Despite his millennia of success and the establishment of no less than two current monarchies largely based on his faith, Thyr has seen a near-continuous decline across the breadth of old Hyperborean lands, especially since the rise of the Eastern god {@deity Mitra|Lostlands|TheLostLands|Mitra}. However, his high priest notes that this decline cannot be fully laid at the feet of the upstart Mitra, because it actually precedes his dramatic appearance to Overking Osbert II seven centuries ago. Rather, High Priest Bofred of Bard's Gate points out that the first hints of the decline had occurred even before the end of the Hyperborean Empire, much less the current decline of the Foerdewaith in recent centuries, pointing to a subtle but pervasive omnipresent diminishment in civilization over this time period. A diminishment that Bofred and others fear may be a harbinger of worse things to come.

name: Tiamat
title: The Mother of Dragons
symbol: Erupting Sun

name: Titan
title: God of Chaos
symbol: A swirling vortex of fractured stone

name: Toldoth
title: Goddess of the living and the Mother of the Deformed
symbol: Onyx Disc

customProperties.Domains: Chaos, Evil, {@class cleric|phb|Death|Death Domain|dmg}, {@class cleric|phb|Destruction|Destruction Domain}, {@class cleric|phb|Madness|Madness Domain}, {@class cleric|phb|War|War Domain}
customProperties.Form of Worship and Holidays: Negative Energy, Darkness, Destruction, Orcs, War, Hate, Envy, Malice, Panic, Ugliness, Slaughter
customProperties.Typical Worshipers: Undead, Gnolls, Medusas, Harpies, Goblins, Minotaurs, Hidden Human Cults, the Insane, Bugbears, Derros, Lamiaa, Morlocks, Ogres

entries: The enemy of the living and the Mother of the Deformed, Toldoth is a dark creature composed of negative energy.
She usually appears as a nightshade or a wraith.
Most followers of Toldoth are monsters, many are undead and few are humanoids, although hidden cults of Toldoth exist throughout many civilized societies.

name: Tormach
title: Arch Daemon of Wrath
symbol: A bull-headed warrior wielding a warhammer
entries: {@i Arch Daemon of Wrath}

The only truth of war is death. The only virtue is to kill. The only victory is to survive. Heroism, honor, and glory are illusions for moralizing cowards. These are the edicts of Tormach, Arch Daemon of wrath and war, who is known by such names as Manslayer and Marauder.

Once a lieutenant of the dead god Maligant, and brother to the Arch Seraph {@deity Empyreus|Etharis|GrimHollowCG24}, Tormach has since forsaken his familial ties to seize the mantle of war god for himself. Tormach gives no praise for strategy or valor. In the Arch Daemon's mind, the only purpose of armed conflict is to kill. Victory itself is unimportant. All that matters is that as much blood is spilled and as much carnage is dealt as is possible, during and after the battle. Tormach is the element of war at its most violent. Every battlefield is an altar to the Arch Daemon of wrath, though his tributes are stolen time and again by the healing light of {@deity Miklas|Etharis|GrimHollowCG24} the Redeemer—a fact that infuriates him to no end.

Depictions of the Arch Daemon show a flaming warrior with a bull's head. Sometimes it's a decapitated head sitting upon a man's shoulders, rivulets of blood running down his scarred chest. Other times, the bull is depicted as Tormach's true face. He rides a chariot pulled by a pair of chimeras and wields his warhammer, the {@i Wrath of Heaven}.

entries.name: Followers
entries: Tormach is a source of strength for many soldiers and militaries. A growing faith among the armies of Unterland honor Tormach as an Arch Seraph, and even noble warriors may invoke his name to draw upon his strength as a war deity. Commoners are nevertheless wary of any who wear his sigil. Tormach's unflinching demand for slaughter twists his truly devout into raging berserkers.

Adventures featuring the Arch Daemon are likely to include clashes with one of his cults. A cadre of soldiers may try to turn their entire legion to Tormach's ideals, or a troupe of bandits might capture civilians and commit blood sacrifices in his name. Bloodthirsty fiends conjured from the Netherworld may join the ranks of a particularly powerful warband or even lead one. Valikan raiders who have forsaken their heritage might invoke the Marauder when taking heads from an unprotected settlement. A serial killer could be motivated by the Manslayer, intoxicated by the scent of their exsanguinated victims.

name: Tsathogga
title: Demon Frog God
symbol: Likeness of the Frog God, carved in soapstone

customProperties.Favored Weapons: Any that slash, cut, and are wickedly curved, as well as, ropes or nets
customProperties.Form of Worship and Holidays: Too gruesome and perverse to describe even by Our standards!
customProperties.Garb: Green and violet robes, if any
customProperties.Typical Worshipers: {@filter Aberration|bestiary|type=Aberration|miscellaneous=!swarm}, tsathar, sentient frogs, evil water monsters, The Violet Brotherhood

entries: This foul frog-demon cares less about the machinations of men and power than he does about obliterating light and life with slow, oozing sickness and decay. He is the vicious dark evil bubbling up from beneath the surface, the foul corruption at the heart of the earth. Making his home on the plane of Tarterus at the mouth of the vast swamp of filth deposited by the River Styx as it flows out of the Abyss, Tsathogga's main form is a colossally bloated humanoid frog with spindly, elongated limbs andfingers. His corpulent body exudes all manner of foul humors and fluids that leak into the vile swamp in which he lies. He has positioned himself so that all of the slime and filth from the River Styx feeds into his gaping, toothy maw. He never moves and rarely speaks other than to emit an unintelligible shrieking. Tsathogga commands a host of evil creatures—notably evil aberrations and his own vile frog race, the tsathar. Thousands of fawning tsathar servants continuously bathe his body in fetid slime from the evil swamp, awaiting the divine bliss of being randomly devoured by him. His hatred of light and lack of human worshippers (though there are a few notable exceptions) mean that he is little known to surface races. He has had few organized centers of worship and no standardized holy symbol—each worshipper choosing its own way to best depict his deific vileness. Occasionally, tsathar priests of Tsathogga on Tarterus sculpt a small likeness of him out of foul chunks of solid waste from the Styx that harden into a vile green substance similar to soapstone when taken from that plane. Such items are prized as holy relics.

name: Tsuki-sama
title: Moon-Night Possessor
entries: A brother of {@deity Tenshō-sama|Seigai Pantheon|KGtSeigai}, and governs the light of the moon. He and Tenshō-sama have an ancient quarrel, hence they are in different parts of the sky.

name: Twilight Sparkle
title: Anticipation of Friendship and Magic
symbol: Six Pointed Magenta Starburst
entries: The main organized religion of the pony nations of Equus involves their alicorn rulers. These are very powerful beings, but they have the personalities of normal ponies and there is lively debate among scholars as to their actual divine status. Most alicorns will deny that they are divine in any way, but their immense power has many ponies convinced. They worship the alicorns as god-rulers and build temples in their name. The alicorns don't seem to do too much to discourage the worship beyond simple declarations, and many leverage their followers to accomplish goals the alicorn champions, for good or ill. The main day of Celestian celebration is the Summer Sun Celebration.

There are also anticipations of future alicorns, prophesied in lost grimoires or ancient tomes that some clerics devote themselves to, such as the Anticipation of Heart or Friendship.  Some fanatics of the Celestial cult consider these heretical cults and are devoted to stamping them out, despite Celestia herself preaching tolerance.

A twisted form of this worship extended to Luna's evil alter-ego, Nightmare Moon.  Some ponies felt that Nightmare Moon was right to want the night to last forever, and after the war that banished their Princess, many cultists still practice in her name.

name: Tyr
title: The God of Justice
symbol: A longsword held upright
entries: The God of Justice is worshiped widely by the humans and dwarves of the Northlands, and his priests can be found among all of the so-called civilized peoples. Though he and his clergy are feared and loathed by the giants and their servitors, even they respect his right to prosecute his responsibilities on the battlefield. Wherever oaths are upheld or blood is spilled in conflict, Tyr is said to walk.

Unlike other gods of war, Tyr does not embrace chaos. His name is often invoked when oaths are sworn or contracts are signed. The duality of war and justice runs through the worship of Tyr. He directs that battle should be used as a means to protect communities from the dangers posed by giants and other agents that work in opposition to orderly society. In times of peace, leaders look to the priesthood of Tyr to guide them to deliver justice for their people and work toward what is best for the greatest number of people.

The sagas tell that Tyr lost his right hand and gained the title the Odd Handed while endeavoring with the Aesir to bind and fetter Fenris, the Twilight Wolf. The truth, however, is somewhat different. To avoid being bound, Fenris played at being tame enough to live in peace with the Aesir. To prove his claim, he urged Tyr to place his hand in the wolf's mouth. Despite his words and true to his monstrous nature, Fenris bit Tyr's hand off and swallowed it in a single gulp. Sometimes the other gods snicker to one another about Tyr's gullibility, though the fierce God of Justice's glares quell the whispers with remarkable speed.

entries.name: Worshipers
entries: Warriors, magistrates, guards, judges, and community leaders pay homage to the Odd Handed. Those who feel they have been treated unfairly call to Tyr for justice and aid, as do duelists and those who seek to redress the wrongs done to them in battle.

Tyr calls on his followers to obey the laws and commands of their jarls, as it is order that separates the hero from the lowly cur. Bring battle to the forces that oppose righteous order. Treat others with hospitality and honor.

entries.name: Symbols And Books
entries: Tyr's symbol is a longsword held upright.

The Law of Sword and Axe holds the tenets of Tyr's faith and serves as a guide to living a good and just life. It is written in a straightforward, if somewhat dry, style that is intended to require little interpretation, though scholars still argue over it as they do everything else. Oaths in the Northlands are often sworn while holding one's left hand to Tyr's holy text.

entries.name: Shrines and Priests
entries: Temples to Tyr are sturdy and workmanlike, more like fortified keeps and armories than the wonders of art and majesty favored by less martial faiths. Though most structures and habitations in the Northlands are built of wood, mud, and moss, Tyr's temples are constructed of stone, if possible. In a siege, they serve as command centers and, if the siege goes poorly, as a final bastion to fall back to. In times of peace, they serve as courthouses and even sometimes as feasthalls.

Priests of Tyr do not shy away from battle, nor do they lust for it. They see that war is just one method by which disputes can be determined and peace can be assured. In larger cities, some priests take on roles as judges and magistrates, ensuring that contracts are fulfilled as promised and that laws are followed to the letter.

name: Tyton
title: the Nightfather
dogma: As day turns to night, so must all things end. Respect the power of death, but fear not the end, for it is part of the Rhythm.
symbol: A wing containing three stars and a crescent moon
entries: Tyton is depicted as an immense black barn owl. It is believed he ushers the night in by spreading his wings over the sky. Tyton also governs time, memory, and death. As the sun must set, so too must the light of life give way to the darkness of the grave. Rather than being seen as a frightful figure, Tyton is looked upon as kind; he greets the old, the frail, and those at the end of their lives as familiar friends, guiding their souls peacefully back into the Great Rhythm, where they will be reborn, in time.

When not occupying the sky, it is believed Tyton resides in the lands of death. Not an afterlife, rather this is a part of the Great Rhythm where everything is cold, dark, and eternally still. His abode lies beyond the parts of the Rhythm associated with life, a divide impossible for mortals to cross. Even other Amaranthine find travel to the lands of death difficult, except for Altus, who resides there with Tyton for most of the year, only leaving to bring winter storms across the land.

In addition to guiding the souls of the dead, Tyton is associated with the coming of old age, and the keeping of memory. When Tyton is invoked at funerals, it is to remember those who have passed, and to recall their lives and deeds. He watches the living, patiently observing all beneath him. Tyton can learn all there is to know of your life by watching your dreams. Because Tyton watches the living from birth to death, he is known as "Father Owl".
Tyton frowns upon those who would seek to enslave the souls of the dead using necromantic magics, and those who would desecrate the tombs of the deceased, as these actions corrupt the natural cycle.

name: Ulimara
entries: One of her messengers is {@creature Dalariel|zorq}.

name: Umbeserno
entries: Umbeserno is a drowsy, nocturnal god among the bearfolk, largely because of his role in hibernation and prophetic dreams. Where Bengta watches over the bearfolk during the day and encourages them to good works, Umbeserno watches over them at night and during the cold months when bearfolk lie dreaming and snoring. The bearfolk think of dreaming as a time of plans and hopes—an optimistic season and a season to gather strength.

Umbeserno is always shown as a large black bearfolk with a crescent mark on his forehead, typically wearing the robes of a shaman and often with his paw holding either an enormous salmon or a rainbow-colored dreamstone. A second popular pose is Umbeserno Dreamlord, which is a sleeping pose surrounded by signs of spring and life: flowers, fish, lightning bolts, comets, and rabbits as his signs and portents.

entries.name: Worshippers
entries: Umbeserno is worshipped primarily by bearfolk, though a few humans and shadow goblins appeal to him for help with bad dreams, mysteries of spring and rebirth, even with questions of marriage or healing. Those who suffer bad dreams call on him to come and take those dreams away, and many matchmakers ask his guidance when finalizing a match between two bearfolk (or two humans—goblins make their own, more complicated arrangements).

entries.name: Symbols and Books
entries: Umbeserno's symbols include the rainbow-colored dreamstone, the leaping salmon, and antlers surrounding a bird's nest (no priest of Umbeserno tells quite the same story of the last one, but it seems to be a bearfolk icon of spring). He has a number of holy books, many called the {@i Book of Dreams}—but there seems to be no standard collection of this sacred text, and while some dreams are always described in a {@i Book of Dreams} (falling, loss of fur, the scent of honey, summer flies), others are only found in some volumes.

entries.name: Shrines and Priests
entries: The largest shrine to Umbeserno is the Snoring Temple in Solvheim where the caverns run deep into the hills: many of the wealthier bearfolk take their winter sleep there or visit with questions of fortunetelling and the like. Smaller temples to Umbeserno are often well-made, circular lodges with clay and whole logs for their walls and grass-covered roofs with a single smoke hole.

Priests of Umbeserno are often mocked as drowsy or slow or spending all their time gazing at constellations or clouds, but most are generous, extremely patient, and hardworking members of their communities, always ready to lend a hand to the faithful. The best-known priest of Umbeserno is Snuffling Tilda, the Keeper of the Hearth at the Snoring Temple in {@book Merrymead|BookOfEbonTides|7|Merrymead, City of Revels}.

entries.name: Masks
entries: Umbeserno is often assumed to be a mask of {@book Gytellisor|BookOfEbonTides|8|Gytellisor}, though sometimes the comparisons are to {@book Ailuros|BookOfEbonTides|8|Ailuros (Bastet)} when the dreaming side dominates. Others believe that Umbeserno is a mask of Wotan, a rather rambling, gentler font of wisdom and persistence.

entries.name: Other Faiths
entries: The followers of {@book Bengta|BookOfEbonTides|8|Bengta the Bear Maiden} get along very well with those of Umbeserno as do those of {@book Ailuros|BookOfEbonTides|8|Ailuros (Bastet)} and even {@book Charun|BookOfEbonTides|8|Charun}. Umbeserno is an enemy of the needless slaughter of {@book the Hunter|BookOfEbonTides|8|The Hunter} and of the fears and terrors of {@book Alquam|BookOfEbonTides|8|Alquam}. {@book Laughing Loki|BookOfEbonTides|8|Laughing Loki} and Umbeserno are often seen as friends surprisingly.

entries.name: What Umbeserno Demands
entries: Dream big and sleep well. Make your plans carefully and be relentless in seeing them through. Watch the world with a sharp eye and a keen nose. Patience will often be rewarded with wisdom. Ponder your choices and always keep your word.

name: Umbrava
title: the Shadowbringer
symbol: Crescent moon
entries: The Shadowbringer, also known as the First Daemon on Xhoria or the head of the Daemons, is one of the two Prime Deities and lord of shadows and darkness. Depicted as a humanoid made of shadows with six dark tendrils as arms.
He was the original ruler over Xhoria during the Age of Dawn. During this time he created five Shadow Titans, of which the names have been lost to time.
He is the patron to the unfortunate warlocks or the many cultists that follow the shadows.

name: Vallus
title: The Goddess of Wisdom
symbol: Golden laurel wreath with five stars
entries: Vallus is revered as the goddess of wisdom. She was once known to travel far and wide, surveying ancient ruins and collecting lore concerning the origins of the land and the fey races. Prayers are offered to Vallus when guidance is needed and information is scarce, and she is believed to know as much about Thylea's history as Sydon and Lutheria. She is the oldest daughter of Mytros and, in many ways, she has inherited her mother's place as patron goddess to the city that bears her name.

Vallus works closely with the priests of Mytros to encourage faith in the Five, even as mortals everywhere fall prey to fear of Sydon and Lutheria. She remains a pillar of strength holding the city together as things are beginning to fall apart elsewhere. However, in spite of her best efforts, the citizens of Mytros increasingly offer prayers and sacrifices to the treacherous Titans. Vallus accepts this with grace and humility, and in spite of her declining power, she will do anything to defend her city.

Vallus has a reputation for conspicuous vanity. She never allows herself to be seen without exquisite, queenly regalia, and she habitually examines her own reflection in a silver hand mirror. This is partly because she understands the importance of appearances in the world of mortal politics—but she is also vain.

Vallus is extraordinarily perceptive, often to the point where she is suspected of mindreading. She always seems to discern truth, even when she is told a clever lie. A hard stare from Vallus is often enough to make even the most skilled liars concede the truth. Vallus has lost much of her faith in the future of Thylea. Although she endeavors to protect the Temple of the Five in Mytros, she has witnessed too much of Thylean history to believe that the Oracle's prophecy will result in anything but total disaster.

Vallus has one regret: her marriage to King Acastus. Over the centuries, she has been intimate with many beautiful mortals who captured her heart, but her union with Acastus in 478 CE was entirely political. The two have grown to hate each over the years, not least because Acastus makes a point of treating his many infidelities as sport. They have no children, although Acastus probably has many unacknowledged bastards.

Vallus's true form is a young bronze dragon, who previously served as a mount for Telamok Arkelander. While Telamok was responsible for almost as many atrocities as his brother Estor, Vallus understands this was part of the cost of settling in Thylea. She is not wracked with the same second-hand guilt that plagues Kyrah.

name: Vallus
title: The Goddess of Wisdom
symbol: Golden laurel wreath with five stars
entries: Vallus is revered as the goddess of wisdom and beauty, and she is believed to know as much about Thylea's history as Sydon and Lutheria. She was once known to travel far and wide, surveying ancient ruins and collecting lore concerning the origins of the land and the fey races. Prayers are offered to Vallus when guidance is needed and information is scarce. She is the oldest daughter of Mytros and, in many ways, she has inherited her mother's legacy, serving as both queen and patron goddess to the city.

name: Vardesain
entries: All creatures hunger, and without food, life ends. Vardesain took this primal need and built a faith ranging from simple gluttony to cannibalistic feasting. Indeed, food is seen as a sacrament that builds life, health, and righteous strength in the faithful, and the followers of the Hunger God can be both great gourmands and the world's least picky eaters. Sacrifices to the god are invariably edible—and sometimes still living.

The god's best-known forms are those of scavengers and predators: white wolves, ghouls, and darakhul, but also undead of abnormal size. In any form, visions, depictions, and avatars of Vardesain are always feeding on something.

entries.name: Worshippers
entries: Vardesain's followers are the hungry and the ambitious: power-hungry humans and monsters, ghouls, vampires, darakhul, and other undead. They have no morals or standards, only instinct.

entries.name: Symbols and Books
entries: Vardesain's holy beast is the purple worm, a creature that devours sacrifices to the god in his temples. When embroidered or painted on vestments, it is shown as a purple snake consuming its own tail or a pair of open jaws. The priests of Vardesain keep bats, serpents, and oozes as living incarnations of hunger.

Their holiest text is actually a series of cave paintings, called{@i the Feast}, rendered in the Shrine of Vardesain in Darakhan, the White City of the Ghoul Empire. These have been copied in the depths of the empire in the city of Zhurahk with new emphasis on the righteous rule of the emperor.

The empire depends on the Feeding Laws, edicts written on scrolls of skin and carried by Vardesain's priests. To disobey the Feeding Laws is to invite divine punishment, though in practice they are frequently broken.

entries.name: Shrines and Priests
entries: The red and white Shrine of Vardesain is the best-known temple below ground. Many ancient monuments to his face as the Lord of Unending Thirst stand at oases in the Southlands. In the Shadow Realm, his rule is a relatively recent arrival, brought in by the darakhul and spread with fervor.

The current high priest among the {@book Twilight Empire|BookOfEbonTides|7|Twilight Empire} is His Carmine Eminence and High Patriarch of Zhurahk, Devros Perghallen, one of the rare few whose hunger has been consumed by Vardesain as a blessing. He currently works to spread the faith of consumption and the power of devouring others and to denounce {@book Bengta|BookOfEbonTides|8|Bengta the Bear Maiden} and {@book Kupkoresh|BookOfEbonTides|8|Kupkoresh}.

entries.name: Masks
entries: The {@book Goat of the Woods|BookOfEbonTides|8|Black Goat of the Woods} and {@book the Hunter|BookOfEbonTides|8|The Hunter} have been suggested as possible masks of Vardesain. Neither is an especially likely candidate. Certainly, {@book Charun|BookOfEbonTides|8|Charun} and {@book Anu-Akma|BookOfEbonTides|8|Anu-Akma} are more associated with Vardesain's Underworld and control over the undead.

entries.name: Other Faiths
entries: {@book Charun|BookOfEbonTides|8|Charun}, the {@book Goat of the Woods|BookOfEbonTides|8|Black Goat of the Woods}, and {@book the Hunter|BookOfEbonTides|8|The Hunter} are allied with Vardesain, though loosely. Lada, {@book Kupkoresh|BookOfEbonTides|8|Kupkoresh}, and {@book Bengta|BookOfEbonTides|8|Bengta the Bear Maiden} all despise Vardesain as worthless and vile, and they seek to destroy his temples at every opportunity. The priesthoods of Vardesain and {@book Anu-Akma|BookOfEbonTides|8|Anu-Akma} are great rivals, but the two gods seem indifferent to this rivalry, leading some to suspect that Vardesain is indeed a mask of Anu-Akma's darker side.

entries.name: What Vardesain Demands
entries: Flesh is weak, but your will is strong—show your strength. Hunt and kill what you eat when you can, but scavenging is not dishonorable. Fast when you must find focus and purity, for your hunger will give you strength to see the way. Devour the hearts of your enemies.

name: Vasi
title: Lady of the Lake, Mother of the Ocean, Pearls of the Mist, Tears of the Eternal Bath
symbol: Cascade of water

customProperties.Favored Weapons: {@item Staff|PHB|Aspergillum as a tall metal staff}
customProperties.Garb/Portfolio: Freshwater, lakes, pools, oases, grottos, springs, peace, life, wisdom
customProperties.Typical Worshipers: Widely worshipped, heavily revered by those in dry areas

entries: {@b Introduction}
{@b History}

Born of a single drop from the Elemental Plane of Water, Vasi came to Aventyr by sheer luck when the original four elementals collided in the vast empty abyss of space. Unaware of her true power and acting only of universal impulse, Vasi embraced earth, fire, and air, to create Aventyr itself, and through this formation, the freshwater with which to rain down and cover the world. While others would end up as caretakers over the brackish depths where earth and water bled too deeply together, Vasi was the guardian of it all.

After she adopted to the needs of those mortals living in Aventyr, and after the Shard of the Sun nearly collided with the planet, Vasi took to caring for those lacking water, sending her clergy into the {@link Scorched Lands|https://adventureaweek.com/campaign-setting/locations/scorched-lands/} to find, save, and possibly convert those who would surely have died in the desert wastes.
{@b Churches, Clergy, and Worshippers}

Vasi's shrines and temples are found near deep grottos and remote mountain lakes, anywhere there is a clean source of freshwater, a small shrine is found nearby. Worshippers are many and their influence spread far and wide in Aventyr, for all need water to survive.

Those who revere the Lady of the Lake frequently help others in need of water and provide safe shelter from the horrors of the world. While outsiders are welcome to cradle in the Tears of the Eternal Bath for a time, they are eventually asked to stay and become priests or leave, back to the world from whence they came.
{@b Holy Text}

{@i The Mi'unin} is a tome born during the reign of the Grekians and when recited by each of the 92 high priests of Vasi at once, in all 92 shrines, and in unison for 92 days and 92 nights, brings about The Great Flood. An event which, in the past, covered large sections of Aventyr in water and even caused the level of the seas to rise.

name: Venin
title: Arch Daemon of Deceit
symbol: A weeping eye with a blue iris and red pupil
entries: {@i Arch Daemon of Deceit}

Venin is the mistress of lies, illusions, and insanity. As an Arch Daemon of supernal deceit, she is known by many names and many faces—Dusktongue, the Hooded One, the Great Deceiver, and many others forgotten by most mortals. She relishes the lies people tell themselves to justify depravity and cruelty. Venin triumphs when objectivity dissolves and mortals scream at each other over whose perceived reality is truth.

The Great Deceiver's schemes are frequently disrupted by {@deity Zabriel|Etharis|GrimHollowCG24}, whose searing light burns away the obscuring darkness. Venin rewards those who assassinate the Arch Seraph's priests.

Venin's true form is unknown. Often, she appears as a towering human wreathed in black furs and shadows. At other times, she's depicted as a hooded figure whose face is a mirror, reflecting a subtly distorted version of the observer. Her voice seems to echo from deep within the listener's head.

entries.name: Followers
entries: Rogues, thieves, and murderers whisper prayers to Venin so that her darkness may conceal their misdeeds. Her hidden cults include assassin guilds, spy networks, and information brokers. Venin's priests are tricksters and orators. They're skilled at convincing others of their versions of the truth, but eventually, even they lose track of what is real and what is not.

name: Verin
title: God of the Underworld
symbol: A black crown above a skull

name: Vesh
title: The Bloody Siren
entries: Blood and pleasure follow in the wake of the siren Vesh. Long has she stalked the shadows of far-off {@book Issylra|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Issylra}, amassing secretive orgies of people of all genders and ancestries. These grand events have a membership that numbers in the hundreds, all of whom are bound to utmost secrecy, and are thrown in obscure retreats that are hidden in cities and towns across the continent. Little do the foolish pleasure-seekers in attendance know that the siren's great fetes of debauchery can end with only two left alive: Vesh and her new mate, who will go on to form a mystical blood-bond.

"Beware the Bloody Siren," sob those few who have escaped her orgy of blood, but their warnings have only fueled her legend. In Tal'Dorei, where Vesh's presence is known only as a legend of a foreign land, her name is most often invoked by youths who want to impress their peers. But who can say what would happen if an attractive and foolish mortal called too fervently or too frequently to the Bloody Siren? Perhaps she would appear, baring her subtly radiant gray skin, stroking her flowing violet hair, and gazing invitingly at the fool with her blank white eyes.

name: Volkan
title: The God of Forges
symbol: Silver anvil wreathed in blue flame
entries: As one of the Five, Volkan is revered as the forge god of artifice and crafting, and he is primarily worshipped by dwarves, smiths, masons, and wizards. For centuries, he has been obsessed with crafting wondrous magical items, but he rarely shares these gifts with the rest of the world. In spite of this, many of his greatest works have been scattered across Thylea, and some have even fallen into the hands of his enemies.

Volkan appears to be an unassuming, grey-bearded old dwarf clad in a blacksmith's apron. He is easily (and perhaps deliberately) overlooked by the locals in his home city of Estoria. He was less humble during the First War, when he was known to don a radiant suit of silver platemail, wear a golden crown, and carry a mighty warhammer. These days, he claims his bones ache too much to participate in battles. He prefers to smoke his pipe near the warmth of the forge-fires, pondering his next invention. He is rumored to travel through the Heartlands on the winter solstice, distributing toys and sweets to children.

Volkan originally came to Thylea as an ancient bronze dragon. In that form, he and Balmytria produced four bronze dragons in the Old World many centuries ago: Kyrah, Pythor, Vallus, and Narsus. Together, the family of dragons became the mounts of the Dragonlords. Volkan had the honor to bond with Rizon Phobas. Volkan cannot transform back into his dragon form until the Oath of Peace ends.

Volkan is known for devising ingenious strategies. He thinks of the world as a puzzle to be solved, and he often works out problems in his head for days or weeks at a time. He may be gruff and silent for long stretches, only to suddenly appear with some miracle device or solution. He delights in creation, rather than destruction, and he is always intrigued by an intricate new device or stratagem.

Volkan changed after the ascension of his wife, Mytros. He was once an affectionate and attentive father, but when he "lost"his wife to her godhood, he grew apart from his children. He eventually came to live almost entirely in his workshop and within his own head. He has also developed a strong affinity for wine, and beer, and mead, and almost any strong drink, all of which he claims inspires his best work.

name: Volkan
title: The God of Forges
symbol: Silver anvil wreathed in blue flame
entries: Not much is known about Volkan except that he is the husband of Mytros. He concerns himself with artifice and crafting and is primarily worshipped by dwarves, smiths, and wizards. He is depicted as an elderly and wise-looking man (and sometimes as a dwarf). He is rumored to travel through the Heartlands on the winter solstice, distributing toys and sweets to children.

name: Volund
title: Master of Fire and Anvil
altNames: God of Horses, Smiths, and Marriage
symbol: Anvil, emblazoned with a horse's head, and weapons (hammer or battleaxe)
entries: Volund is the god of earth and fire, of the hammer's ring as it lands upon the anvil and the hiss of steam as a new-forged sword is quenched. He is one of the divine patrons of the reaver dwarves, but many others revere him as a paragon artisan and lord of all the jewels and precious metals in the earth. Though primarily a god of fire, creation, and smith work, Volund is also the god of family and hospitality, especially among humans. As a hammer has two heads, the Master of Fire and Anvil has inspired the crafting of potent magical items, but he has also inspired ancient, cursed relics that still linger in the world into the present day.

The Smith God appears as a bald, powerfully built dwarf with a long red beard divided into braids set with metal clasps and rings. In statues and iconography, he is always shown wearing practical clothes that match the rare reports of visions of the god. His wide belt is festooned with all manner of smithing and crafting tools.

entries.name: Worshipers
entries: The followers of Volund are typically smiths, craftspeople, artists, and reavers, but anyone who feels the fierce joy of creation and crafting can find a place among Volund's faithful. Those who venerate the Smith God often wear an anvil-shaped pin or amulet.

Volund demands his followers craft great works in his name and harness stone, metal, and fire to their will. He encourages forming bonds within a community (such as blood-oaths and marriages). Some humans add expertise in riding to his divine edicts. His faithful makes pilgrimages to shrines and temples far and wide, especially to the major forge-shrines, adding something, no matter how small, that they have personally wrought to every shrine they visit.

entries.name: Symbols and Books
entries: The symbols of Volund are his anvil, emblazoned with a horse's head, and his weapons, the hammer among humans and the battleaxe among dwarves. He is associated with the Kaunen rune. His holy writings are the Book of the Anvil and the Saga of Volund's Wanderings, both concerned with tempering steel and souls.

Clerics at his temples turn each liturgy into crafting sessions where circles of priest-smiths sing hymns from Volund's Wanderings as they hammer. The anvils of the major forge-shrines are tuned to ring out different notes and chords, creating a ritual effect that transforms items into Volund's songsteel.

entries.name: Shrines and Priests
entries: Volund is one of the most widely worshiped gods, with major temples across the Northlands and more in southern lands. The greatest of his forge-shrines is Stannasgard's Shrine of a Thousand Anvils, which is a popular pilgrimage destination. Those seeking Volund's blessing bring ingots of metal for the creation of new anvils.

On days holy to Volund, his priests work at an ever-burning forge, their hammers striking in unison like a monk's plainchant. The greatest of Volund's clerics include the aggressive Opir Skapti (human warpriest), priest-captain of the young dwarven company of the Hall of Spears in Stannasgard.

name: Vraigoroth
title: Kindred of Devouring
entries: {@i Kindred of Devouring}

Vraigoroth is thought of as an enormous maw, ringed with fangs, that sucks all light and energy into itself, returning all existence to darkness. Others imagine it to be an unfathomable tumor, a growing mass of wriggling flesh with veinlike tendrils extending into reality, transmogrifying everything it touches into more of itself. Nobody truly knows its shape. It gnaws at the edges of existence, digesting in the dark.

Polyps of Vraigoroth bubble into the mortal realm wherever it has chewed a hole through reality. This can happen anywhere—deep within an unexplored cave, inside a dusty abandoned structure, or through the living flesh of a mortal host. These amorphous horrors twist and grow. They dissolve any organic matter they come into contact with, amalgamating it into their mass and growing in size as they consume. Unless destroyed, these nightmarish creatures can reach truly terrifying proportions.

Worshippers of Vraigoroth believe they've learned and accepted a horrifying truth—everything that exists was once part of this entity, and shall be again. The cycle has repeated endlessly. The devouring is inevitable. Therefore, Vraigoroth should be praised and its hunger fed. Once all of reality has been returned to its amalgamated mass, all suffering will end.

It's not always clear whether followers of Vraigoroth are terrified or jubilant at their patron's devouring. Warlocks who siphon some of the Aether Kindred's power tend to become gorgers themselves, entire settlements going missing as the arcanist consumes everyone and everything that comes within its grasp. Inevitably, they're transformed into another amorphous polyp of Vraigoroth itself.

name: Wotan
title: All Father
altNames: God of the Tree and Raven
King of Asgard and Lord of Valhalla
symbol: The world tree Yggdrasil, the single eye, and the runes
entries: The most powerful of the Aesir, Wotan led the gods to defeat Aurgelmir at the dawn of time, carving up the body of the first giant to make the world, and so he earned the enmity of all giantkind. He rewards the heroic dead with a place at his table and is the patron of proud and ruthless kings. Ravens fly across the world to bring him news and rumors, and from his enchanted throne he can spy upon all creation. He plucked out his own eye in return for wisdom, and when that wasn't enough, he hung himself from the Tree of Worlds, stealing secrets from the Void beyond existence. He is the god of strife, chieftains, and kings, master of runes and stealer of wisdom. Wotan's superior cunning and wisdom ensures he triumphs time and time again, until Ragnarok swallows the world.

Wotan appears as a dour, powerfully built, older man with long, grey hair and a flowing beard. He wears patched and somewhat ragged clothing in shades of blue, grey, and brown. Often, he has a raven on each shoulder and a pair of wolves by his side. All depictions of Wotan show his missing right eye.

entries.name: Worshipers
entries: Wotan is most beloved by jarls, wizards, and those who value wisdom. Among dwarves, the worship of Wotan the All-Father represents a step in life, beyond callow youth and into maturity and middle age. Older men and dwarves proclaim their loyalty at his shrines and feed his ravens bread, but some women revere Wotan as well, for the swift news his ravens bring or for the power of rune magic. In addition, Wotan has many followers among the ravenfolk. They see him as the greatest of figures, for his servants are feathered and wise, and Wotan is as wily as every ravenfolk wishes to be.

Wotan demands his followers be wise, canny in judgment, skilled in poetry, and quick to lead in honorable battle. Cowards and fools find no sympathy from the Rune God. Warriors pray to him, hoping to earn luck and victory in battle, or if defeat is fated, they pray to attract the attention of his Valkyries and a place in Valhalla.

entries.name: Symbols and Books
entries: Wotan's symbols are many, including the world tree Yggdrasil, the single eye, and the runes. Sometimes his favored animals, ravens and wolves, are taken as his sign as well. Wotan's two ravens are named Huginn (Thought) and Muninn (Memory), and his wolves are named Freki (Greedy) and Geri (Ravenous).

Writing is Wotan's favored form of recording wisdom. He expects all his followers to be literate so they may read his many sacred texts. Among these, the most prominent are the Lay of Mimir, the Tree of Knowledge, and the scroll called the Secret Runes. Fiercely guarded in the heart of Runaskr is the only known copy of Aldrunir—"Giant Magics of the First Age"—which contains lost enchantments Wotan seized from the jotun before the world was made.

entries.name: Shrines and Priests
entries: The greatest shrine of Wotan is in the dwarven hall of Stannasgard, where the chanting of the rune chorus never ceases, and the altar fires burn in his honor. This accolade may soon shift to the Hall of the Watching Eye in Wolfheim, which will be the largest temple to Wotan in the North once it is completed.

The kings and captains of the dwarven reavers are Wotan's priests or at least his devoted worshipers. His priests wear raven feathers to honor him. Possibly the greatest of his clerics is Brokk Kolisen of the Shrine of the Gallows Tree (Trollheim), a black-bearded human raised among dwarves, and loved and respected for his understanding of their ways. He leads many expeditions to fight giants in Jotunheim.

name: Xaylene Xeranos
title: God of Merchants
symbol: A coin stamped with a shifting sigil

name: Yenomesh
title: God of Glyphs and Writing
symbol: A gleaming silver scroll

customProperties.Form of Worship and Holidays: Worship is through study, teaching, and learning. The last day of the week (Thingsdag) is given over to quiet contemplation. Monastic orders of Yenomesh set aside the High Holy Days of the Cusp of Freya (vernal equinox) and the Cusp of Mithras (autumnal equinox) for day-long ceremonies that take place in total silence.
customProperties.Garb: Gray scribes' robes
customProperties.Typical Worshipers: Loremasters, {@class wizard|phb|wizards}, scribes, authors, historians

entries: Yenomesh is the aged sage of the gods. He is said to have been the first to gain knowledge of the sacred runes of the Language Eternal which he taught to the gods and elevated them from the Original Chaos. Likewise it was he who created the written characters of the language known as Foundation, allowing the concepts of the Language Eternal to be grasped by mortal minds and brought the light of knowledge to the world. He is likewise credited with being the inventor of all written language since it is derived from the characters of Foundation, and his priests are often fluent in writing and speaking many different tongues. For his role in imparting knowledge upon the mortal races, libraries and archives are often dedicated to Yenomesh, and many have at least one small shrine in his honor.

Despite the universality of Yenomesh's contributions to the world in the form of writing, he was not always considered to be a part of the Hyperborean pantheon. Originally Yenomesh was found only in the ancient religions of the East. It was during the Hyperborean expansion into Libynos some three-and-a-half thousand years ago that the West encountered the monastics of Yenomesh. They later recognized the value and contributions of the Yenomeshi faith when Hyperborean scholarship realized that all known languages were derived from a script that the monastics used to write their own scrolls. As scholars practiced in the arcane arts discovered that this Foundation language also served as the basis for magical writings, western wizards began to show interest in the faith as well. Yenomesh has never had sufficient popularity among magical practitioners that it threatened the faith of {@deity Jamboor|Lostlands|TheLostLands|Jamboor} or later {@deity Belon the Wise|Lostlands|TheLostLands|Belon the Wise}, but he has also had a small and devoted following of these spellcasters who delve deeply into the mysteries of alternate forms of magical writing.

name: Yōnō-sama
entries: The goddess of fertility and agriculture. Yōnō-sama has a close relationship with the kitsune, and is often depicted with a fox-like appearance. She is the most widely venerated {@i kami} in Seigai.

name: Zabriel
title: Arch Seraph of Truth
symbol: A giant eye, the iris shaped like a keyhole, wreathed by countless pairs of angel wings
entries: {@i Arch Seraph of Truth}

All shadows and deceits are stripped bare by Zabriel's all-seeing eye. The Watcher inherited her domain from the goddess of knowledge, Typharia, for whom Zabriel acted as librarian. Now, truths are the only knowledge the Arch Seraph considers worth keeping. Lies, euphemisms, allegories, and folktales are of no interest to Zabriel, who believes ignorance on any scale is a dangerous weapon in the hands of tyrants and deceivers.

Zabriel's enemies are spies, assassins, and illusionists. These cunning operators, shrouded by {@deity Venin|Etharis|GrimHollowCG24}, the Arch Daemon of deceit, spread disruption and misinformation supports harmful conspiracies and oppressive regimes. Ignorance is a chain around society's neck. Truth is the key to liberation.

It's said that Zabriel disguises herself as a robed figure to treat with mortals. Her face glows so brightly from beneath her hood that her features cannot be seen, and she carries a tome with the names of every being in existence scribed inside. The Watcher's true form is that of a giant eye, the iris shaped like a keyhole, wreathed by countless pairs of angel wings.

entries.name: Followers
entries: Churches devoted to Zabriel are places of learning. The Arch Seraph's priests are studious and generous with their knowledge, wishing to spread the light of understanding among the folk of Etharis as widely as possible. If a priest does not know an answer, they usually know where to look.

However, among the Watcher's adherents, their predilection for the truth can outweigh their sense of nuance or morality. Zabriel's inquisitors hunt criminals and spies with clinical tenacity, never mind the reasons for the crime. Artificers pray to Zabriel for a flash of inspiration, hoping it will lead them to a new revelation. They plunge into the depths of science without regard for ethics or safety.

name: Zagnexis
symbol: Insect Insignia
entries: {@b Introduction}
{@b History}

This otherworldly god is much like the hoyrall once were—a massive hive mind. More than a physical being, as the insectoids came to dominate the planet of the alien god's origin, Zagnexis manifested as the congealed consciousness of their dead. While the other intelligent lifeforms on that world fought valiantly, with a deific being directing the racial hive mind of the hoyrall, they quickly came to rule over all that the insect god could perceive.

Until the Great Schism. The progenitors, cast down from their once mythic forms into the lowly race now known as the draaki, made a desperate cry to the cosmos and it was Zagnexis that answered their plea. Mustering the unimaginable power granted from the complete devotion of an entire race of creatures, the insect god transported his entire physical for into Aventyr—Zagn, along with tens of thousands of hoyrall—directly across the universe and into the Dracoprime's skull, killing the draconic monstrosity instantly.

For some generations, Exis continued to direct its children on Aventyr, growing a massive army within the fortress-hives of the hoyrall in preparation for an all-out assault to conquer both the surface and the Underworld. Were it not for the intervention of the colloid during The Confluence, it surely would have succeeded. The other alien entity seized upon Exis conduit to its children, breaking the hive mind of the hoyrall and sending its physical counterpart, Zagn, careening into the oceans of Aventyr to wreck havoc upon everything it meets.

Since then, Exis has retained what connections it can to Aventyr, granting powers to its clerics and oracles but little more. The alien god wants nothing more than to expand and procreate, increasing its deific power by generating a second world of followers. Exis is avaricious and without regard for the general balance of natural powers; it will stop at nothing to re-establish its hold over both Zagn and the hoyrall before consuming all of Aventyr.
{@b Appearance}

Exis is a spectral insect composed of dozens of different arthropods, its countless limbs, heads, eyes and antennae constantly morphing into new shapes or variations. Zagn is an enormous, multi-headed (and multi-mouthed) segmented worm with thousands upon thousands of legs that span a body measured by miles.
{@b Church of Zagnexis}

Temples, churches and shrines devoted to the alien god are commonly found throughout the fortress-hives of the hoyrall and honeycombed into Upperworld mountains, but most are in terrible states of disrepair. The unrest following The Confluence led to the dissolution of hoyrall society, and the sites of worship to the god that once bound them all together were quickly targeted by dissenters and ne'er-do-wells. New churches to Zagnexis are well-appointed and carefully kept, tiled with the carapace of insects in exquisite mosaics that depict the journey of the hoyrall.
{@b Holy Text}

There is no written or oral tradition to the worship of Zagnexis; lesser followers are taught the rites of worship through nonverbal communication (through limbs or antennae), and acolytes meld their minds with greater priests in ritual-driven meldings of the minds. Only this devout form of communication is fit for the transmission of the holiest information known to the worshippers of the insect god.

name: Zarin
title: God of War
symbol: A blood‑red shield marked with a single slash

name: Zephyr
title: The West Wind
symbol: Brass Wing
entries: The Griffons pantheon consists mainly of the four wind gods. Boreas the North Wind, Zephyr the West Wind, Auster the South Wind and Eurus the East Wind.  Boreas is a cold harsh wind that brings storms and victory in battle. Zephyr is a warm gentle wind that soothes and calms. Auster is a wind that brings rain to water crops, or withholds it to starve the unpious. Eurus is a hot stifling wind that carries plague.

name: Zhizuna
title: the Web-Weaver
symbol: Spider with a cross on its back
entries: Zhizuna is the deity over the afterlife. Depicted as a spider with a green glowing cross on its back.

She is ruler over the Weave, the large web of life and death that spans over the Xhorian Multiverse. To create life is to weave from the web, and to die is to be woven back into the web. The Weave is also the force that keeps the planes together. Magic, both divine and arcane, uses the Weave.
She is the patron to many doctors, clerics and priests.

name: Zotek
title: the Mutator
symbol: Two claw marks
entries: Zotek was the first kroxelhua in Xhoria, his thick black scales and enormous body did not go unnoticed by Umbrava. After Lumen touched Lykor, Umbrava retaliated by ascending Zotek to divinity, making him the destructive force of nature on Xhoria. Zotek created many monstrosities and is often the cause of storms and harsh weather.
He is the patron of most Coatl in Xhoria, who see him as the one and only deity.

name: Zuriel
title: the Second Twin
symbol: Angel holding an orb low
entries: Zuriel was the twin brother of Asteran, the First Twin. After both being touched by Lumen, they became lords over angels. He is depicted as a male angel with 3 sets of dark black wings. Umbrava managed to corrupt Zuriel, causing him to become filled with greed. Zuriel wanted to have more than both of them combined and thus betrayed his brother Asteran. He wounded Asteran, but was not able to kill him. Lumen doomed Zuriel, causing him to fall from divinity and now live in the shadow of his brother.
